newsitem.title: USA: Mass. man arrested in "Big Dig" payoff scandal.
newsitem.headline: Mass. man arrested in "Big Dig" payoff scandal.

text.p: A West Newton, Mass. man was arrested by the FBI on Thursday and charged with extortion for accepting a $4,000 cash payoff related to the $10.7 billion "Big Dig" highway construction project in downtown Boston.

Morteza Sonbolian, 52, an engineer for Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff, allegedly solicited a payoff in July from a construction company executive working on Boston's Third Harbor/Central Artery Project, widely known as the "Big Dig".
The "Big Dig" is considered the largest infrastructure project in the United States and will not be fully complete until well into the next century.
The executive, Thomas O'Connor, president of his own company, notified the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and subsequent conversations with Sonbolian were video or tape recorded.

Sonbolian, who also works as a representative for the Massachusetts Highway Department, told O'Connor his company was eligible for $33,775 in interest because the department was late in making payments.
Sonbolian later asked O'Connor if "there is anything you can do for me" and then said that he wanted "five grand."
O'Connor agreed to pay him $4,000 and the two met at his construction company last week, where a video camera recorded the transaction.
The maximum penalty for extortion is 20 years incarceration and a $250,000 fine.
